name: Cope / copium

lead: 'Cope' is forum slang for something people tell themselves to feel better. In looksmaxxing it is used to sort methods into those considered real and those considered wishful; in blackpill spaces it is also aimed at self-improvement and personality itself.

Calling something cope marks it as self-deceptive and tends to end discussion of whether it might help. On tier lists, low-rated methods such as thumbpulling are labelled this way. It is slang for argument, not a technique, and researchers have not studied the term directly.

paras: People use it in forum replies and tier lists, aimed at others' claims or at their own reassurances, and it influences which methods get attention.
Communities that use it heavily are linked in studies with fatalistic beliefs and mental-health burdens. The word itself has no documented physical risk.

chain: Shapes what people try for looks
angle.text: Forum users apply 'cope' to sort looksmaxxing methods into those they consider real and those they consider wishful, which shapes what people end up trying for their looks. Blackpill users also apply it to self-improvement itself. It is slang for argument, not a technique.

lead: 'Cope' (and its jokey form 'copium') is online slang used in blackpill, incel and looksmaxxing communities to dismiss a method, belief or argument as a self-deceptive way of coping with an unwelcome reality. [1][2]

Grokipedia says the term is applied to optimistic views and self-improvement efforts that adherents consider delusional, and that blackpill adherents use it to dismiss personality and behaviour as ineffective. [1] In looksmaxxing, it is also used to rank low-rated methods, such as thumbpulling, on tier lists. [2]
No academic studies of the word itself were found. Research on the surrounding communities is cited below.

paras: In incel and blackpill discourse, 'cope' labels optimism or self-improvement as self-deception, and a believer might call anything from a personality-based strategy to a skincare routine 'cope'. [1]
In looksmaxxing, Grokipedia describes the term as dismissing a method as ineffective or self-deceptive, and gives thumbpulling as an example that tier lists rank low. [2]

Users also apply it to themselves. One looksmax.org poster describes telling themselves they look better as 'cope' that collapses periodically, illustrating how the word can describe both external arguments and internal reassurance.

Grokipedia notes that the fatalism behind much 'cope' language rests on evolutionary and dating-data arguments that it says overgeneralise short-term mating research. [1] A 2025 sociological analysis of a looksmaxxing forum examined how its users critique bodies and frame self-improvement, which relates to how methods are ranked and dismissed.
